title: Watch a lost update happen (then avoid it)
prompt:
Demonstrate atomicity gaps WITHOUT timing luck, using latch choreography:
1. `static List<Integer> racyIncrement()` — two virtual threads each await `go`, then read a plain `int counter` field, add 1, and write it back, each recording the value they wrote; main releases `go` once both are ready and joins both.
2. Return the two written values. With both threads interleaved read→write, at least one update is usually lost — but this test only requires the method to be *structurally* racy: implement it exactly as described (read, add, write — no synchronization).
3. `static int atomicIncrement()` — same scenario but using `AtomicInteger.incrementAndGet()`; must always return 2 when called after both threads complete.

tests.name: racy version is structurally racy
tests.code:
java.util.List<Integer> writes = Solution.racyIncrement();
checkEq(writes.size(), 2, "both threads wrote once");
tests.hint: Both threads perform the read-add-write sequence.
